summary: The team is pivoting promotion decisively toward China-based programs — Asia Start and Intelligent China — while finalizing the knowledge website redesign and clearing a lingering email lockout that's blocking coordination.
summaryDetail: The dominant push right now is the China-first marketing pivot: Asia Start and Intelligent China are the top promotion priorities, with the Berkeley program as a possible third, while US partnerships (Stanford, Columbia) are shelved for Q1. Asia Start is the most active thread — Joseph is finishing the videos and translating the Marcom stats video into English, Jennifer is tracking the Beijing photography/classroom change and following up on campaign results and the April 2027 setup, and the team still needs to analyze participant profiles and CRM leads to lock target segments, plus Joseph owes a conversion-tracking brief so measurement is trustworthy. The knowledge website redesign is converging: keep the current design with menu categorization as the main change, borrow Joseph's editorial layout to surface more articles and BCI/BSI indices, disperse videos by topic rather than a standalone section, and hold a 30-minute working session to mark feedback (Joseph to share his HTML, Joker to implement). This week's housekeeping is urgent but mundane — the Outlook lockout needs a full password reset and re-login across all devices and a check with JSB on backend unlock before work stalls. Looking ahead, Xuan is lining up the UNICON 2028 host letter for Dean Haitao, the European Chamber Nov 13 Shanghai speaker list, and research on Principle Global, while the team weighs meeting Pulse during their Dec 14–18 China visit and Kaylee sends the SwissCham note on the Sino-Swiss Economic Forum Knowledge Partner role.

Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for promotion, with Berkeley program as a potential third priority.
